status: DRAFT — drives the V7 preview only. V6 (investment_policy.json, allocation_targets.json, v6_engine.py) stays live until the switch is flipped.
source: docs/INVESTMENT-THESIS-V2-DRAFT.md, rounds 1-11, 2026-09-13. Every rule here was stated by Neel in that conversation; anything Claude inferred is marked assumption.

long_term.rule: Market cap $1T or more, or an explicit override. Never sold. Income from dividends and covered calls. No puts, except to re-enter after a call assignment.

overrides.AMD: Neel 2026-09-13: long-term although $843B — 'it is getting there'. Same override as 2026-07-23.
overrides.IBIT: A fund on Bitcoin, itself over $1T — long-term by the asset, not the wrapper.
overrides.SPCX: SpaceX proxy; the core half of the thesis with AAPL and TSLA.

calls.delta: 10-15 (taxable 10-15, sheltered 15) — income without getting called away
calls.otm_pct_taxable: retired 2026-09-16 — see knobs lt_delta_* and vol_*
calls.entry_timing: Settled 2026-09-16: V6's 'declining, needs two +3% sessions' gate is retired. A long-term call waits only while (a) a bounce-wait after a dip buy-back is running, (b) the name is >= mr_threshold_pct below its 10-day average (a call sold at the bottom caps the recovery), or (c) the TSLA RSI carve-out. Otherwise sell.

stuck_calls.rule_1: Roll weekly, same strike, for a credit. Never pay intrinsic to get out.
stuck_calls.rule_2: Buy back on the dip — time value is not penalty. If spot is under the strike mid-week and the call is mostly time value, close it and sell fresh calls on the bounce.
stuck_calls.rule_3: The roll immediately before an ex-dividend date goes 3-4 weeks out, same strike, so time value on the day before ex-div exceeds the dividend and early exercise does not take the shares.
stuck_calls.operating_assumption: What goes up comes down. The system does not plan for a stock that runs $330 -> $350 -> $370 without a dip.
stuck_calls.rule_4_when_to_roll: Neel, 2026-09-15. Roll THURSDAY by default; Friday morning if RSI > 70; immediately if the expiring contract's time value is <= $0.10/share (early-exercise floor) or the ex-dividend rule applies. Never Friday afternoon. Why: the same-strike credit is TV(next) - TV(this); TV(this) decays fastest in its last days so the credit grows through the week (AAPL $315: ~$0.75 Tue -> ~$0.98 Thu), and every un-rolled day is a day the dip can settle it for free. Rolling out early (or 2 weeks) leaves an at-the-money call to buy back at maximum time value when the dip comes - the fatter 2-week credit is the market paying for exactly that risk. Down moves early in the week are waited out, not rolled.

puts.rule: Neel 2026-09-17: 'we should be selling puts on anything and everything as long as it has high volatility and I can earn.' Puts are allowed on long-term names; the put universe is every holding, ranked by return per unit of risk. If assigned, the shares are held (long-term book). The earlier 'no puts on long-term names' rule (2026-09-13) is retired.
puts.buy_gaps: Filled by buying shares from trim proceeds; a put on a long-term name that assigns is a fine way to fill one too.
puts.reentry: Retired 2026-09-20 as a separate card: a called-away long-term name is a put candidate like any other (ranking + capacity), not an automatic re-entry.

long_term.decided_out: TSM, AMZN, META — out of the long-term book (Neel, 2026-09-20); moved to put_only. No buy program in V7: the way into A is a put from bucket C that assigns.

short_term.rule: A named list. No long thesis. Return from calls on owned shares and puts sold against cash and margin. Chosen because their volatility pays.

calls.rule: Between delta 20 and 40; the technicals pick the number. Low RSI -> nearer 20 (the bounce is coming). Never at the money. No difference between shares that arrived by assignment and shares bought outright.
calls.otm_pct_by_delta: retired 2026-09-16 — strike now comes from the name's realized volatility (see knobs vol_*)
calls.example: INTC assigned at $90: delta 10 ~ $100 (the long-term treatment), delta 20 ~ $98, Neel would go ~ $95, not $92-93.
calls.bounce_wait: Neel 2026-09-15: Rule B's bounce-wait applies to the short-term book too — after a dip buy-back, wait +bounce_pct or bounce_days before selling the next call.

stuck_calls.rule: Neel, 2026-09-20. An ITM short-term call is decided on the Thursday of expiry week: if the same-strike roll pays no credit → LET ASSIGN (never pay a debit). If it pays: RSI ≥ st_assign_rsi → ROLL (overbought; patience — the run is likely to come back under the strike); RSI below → LET ASSIGN (not stretched; the same money earns more as a put on the next-ranked name). Assignment is the normal exit in this book — no planned_assignments entry.
stuck_calls.after_assignment: Not an automatic re-entry. The name goes back into the put ranking (which put makes money; would assignment unbalance the 20% book — the per-name cap) and is picked when it earns the slot. SOXL/INTC capped today, CBRS/MRVL not.

puts.rule: Puts are bucket C, not part of the 20%. Universe = every name in either book plus put_only; ranked by return per unit of risk; sized to each account's undeployed line. Per-name balance check: no new put on a short-term name that would be >= st_max_symbol_pct_of_book of the short-term book if assigned.
puts.strike_assumption: Settled 2026-09-16: put delta is the mirror of the call rule (depressed/oversold → closer put, extended → farther), vol-scaled; candidates ranked by weekly yield ÷ volatility with a depressed bonus.
puts.entry: V6 Tier-2 entry kept: RSI < 50 favourable, > 65 unfavourable.
puts.throttle: Retired 2026-09-20: a short-term book at or above 20% no longer blocks new puts — the put bucket is bounded by the margin lines; B drifting over 20% is a layer-4 notice, and short-term calls assigning is how it comes back.

split_target._note: Shares only (Neel, 2026-09-20): A long-term shares 80%, B short-term shares 20%. Put collateral never counts toward either. short_term_pct is mirrored by the knob short_term_cap_pct; the knob wins in the engine.

margin.use: The put bucket (C). The two lines — $250K Neel, $150K Jaya — are what sells puts, on long-term names, short-term names and the put_only list alike. Margin drawn by SHARES is the abnormal state (layer 4).
margin.recovery: When margin is drawn by shares (not puts), the system says 'Margin drawn by $X — sell about $X of stock to return to normal' and stops. Which position is Neel's call. No urgency: the only cost is put income (~2%/mo) becoming call income (~1%/mo) on that amount.

ex_dividend_estimates._note: Next ex-dividend dates for long-term names with a dividend worth more than a deep-ITM weekly's time value. AVGO is from Robinhood fundamentals (2026-09-11); the rest are projected from the last quarterly date and must be confirmed in the week before.

planned_assignments._note: Calls Neel has DECIDED to let assign — the long-term book's one exit: a trim he chose, usually to repay margin (layer 4 says 'sell about $X'; this is where the pick is recorded). The engine says LET ASSIGN for these instead of ROLL, and reminds about tax lots. Remove an entry once it has assigned.

runaway_theses._note: Neel, 2026-09-15. A discretionary override of the technicals: Neel bought back a call on a long-term name (paying real time value) because non-technical reasons — news, structure — say the stock is about to run. RSI cannot be the trigger (it is already high before a runaway and stays high during one; V6 philosophy §6). So the thesis is DECLARED here, the engine stops selling calls on the symbol, and the thesis RESOLVES when the price is up `release_pct` from the declaration price (the run happened — sell the next call up there) or `release_days` trading days pass (it did not — resume income), whichever comes first. Remove or let it expire; the engine marks resolved entries. A thesis is about DISTANCE, not the symbol (Neel, 2026-09-15): only calls whose DELTA is at or above runaway_uncap_delta are uncap candidates — distance, time and the name's volatility together. A $10 gap with 2 days left is a normal call; the same gap with 9 days left is a risk. Re-evaluated every run. Release thresholds are the knobs runaway_release_pct / runaway_release_days.

knobs._note: Every tunable number the V7 engine uses, in one place, editable from the gear icon on the V7 page (GET/PUT /strategies/v7/knobs). The engine reads this file on every run, so a change applies to the next build. Neel, 2026-09-15: 'these numbers are knobs we will adjust in the future.' Edits are written back here so git shows every change.

lt_delta_taxable.label: Long-term call delta, taxable
lt_delta_taxable.description: Target delta for a long-term call in a taxable account (income without getting called away).

lt_delta_sheltered.label: Long-term call delta, sheltered
lt_delta_sheltered.description: Target delta in an IRA / Roth / HSA.

lt_delta_tsla.label: TSLA call delta
lt_delta_tsla.description: TSLA carve-out (fires only above the RSI gate).

lt_tsla_rsi_gate.label: TSLA RSI gate
lt_tsla_rsi_gate.description: Sell a TSLA call only when RSI is above this.

roll_tv_floor.label: Roll-now time-value floor
roll_tv_floor.description: Roll an ITM call immediately once the expiring contract's time value per share is at or below this — early-exercise risk, nothing left to wait for.

roll_stretch_rsi.label: Stretch-to-Friday RSI
roll_stretch_rsi.description: Above this RSI the roll waits until Friday morning instead of Thursday (the dip is more likely).

exdiv_lookahead_days.label: Ex-dividend lookahead
exdiv_lookahead_days.description: Within this many days of an ex-dividend date, the roll goes long instead of weekly.

exdiv_roll_weeks.label: Ex-dividend roll length
exdiv_roll_weeks.description: How many weeks out the pre-ex-dividend roll goes.

dip_move_pct.label: Dip: today's move
dip_move_pct.description: A day move at or below this counts as a dip (Rule B: buy back, wait for the bounce, sell higher).

dip_rsi.label: Dip: RSI below
dip_rsi.description: Or RSI below this counts as a dip.

cheap_captured_pct.label: Cheap: premium captured
cheap_captured_pct.description: A call this far captured is cheap enough to close on a dip.

bounce_pct.label: Bounce: price up
bounce_pct.description: After a dip buy-back, sell the next call once the stock is this far above the buy-back day's close.

bounce_days.label: Bounce: max wait
bounce_days.description: …or after this many trading days uncovered, whichever comes first.

runaway_release_pct.label: Runaway: release on price
runaway_release_pct.description: A declared runaway thesis resolves when the stock is this far above the declaration price.

st_rsi_low.label: Short-term calls: RSI → delta 20
st_rsi_low.description: RSI below this → delta 20 (the bounce is coming).

st_rsi_high.label: Short-term calls: RSI → delta 40
st_rsi_high.description: RSI above this → delta 40; between → delta 30.

st_delta_min.label: Short-term delta floor
st_delta_min.description: After volatility scaling, never below this.

st_delta_max.label: Short-term delta ceiling
st_delta_max.description: After volatility scaling, never above this.

put_rsi_favourable.label: Put entry: RSI favourable below
put_rsi_favourable.description: Retired 2026-09-16 — put entry is now the return/risk ranking; kept for reference.

put_rsi_unfavourable.label: Put entry: RSI unfavourable above
put_rsi_unfavourable.description: Retired 2026-09-16 — put entry is now the return/risk ranking; kept for reference.

put_min_capacity.label: Put: minimum capacity
put_min_capacity.description: Below this much undeployed capacity, no put card for the account.

put_max_contracts.label: Put: max contracts per card
put_max_contracts.description: Position is sized to the account's undeployed capacity, up to this many contracts per card.

short_term_cap_pct.label: Short-term book cap
short_term_cap_pct.description: Target share of the portfolio held as short-term SHARES (bucket B). Above it, a layer-4 notice; no longer blocks puts (2026-09-20).

vol_reference_pct.label: Volatility scaling: reference vol
vol_reference_pct.description: Short-term call delta = RSI base × (this ÷ the name's 20-day realized vol), clamped to the window. 65% ≈ the short-term list's median. A name twice as volatile gets half the delta — no per-name settings (Neel, 2026-09-16).

vol_lookback_days.label: Volatility scaling: lookback
vol_lookback_days.description: Trading days of closes used for realized volatility, the 10-day average uses half of it.

mr_threshold_pct.label: Mean reversion: distance from 10-day average
mr_threshold_pct.description: At least this far BELOW the 10-day average → base delta 20 (the bounce is the trade); this far ABOVE → base 40. Between → RSI decides.

cost_floor_enabled.label: Cost-basis floor on call strikes
cost_floor_enabled.description: 1 = never sell a call below the position's average cost (V6's rule). 0 = off. Neel, 2026-09-15: 'preserving my cost basis is a vanity metric' — the goal is weekly option income without too much risk; the delta picks the strike, not the basis.

rule_b_min_dte.label: Dip buy-back: minimum days to expiry
rule_b_min_dte.description: Rule B fires only with at least this many days left on the call — inside the last days Rule A owns it (hold, roll Friday). SPCX $160 with 3 days left and 11% of room: leave it.

free_close_captured_pct.label: Dip buy-back: free-close threshold
free_close_captured_pct.description: …unless the call is this far captured — closing is effectively free (SOXL $150 at 98%, NVDA $240 at 96%), so Rule B may fire regardless of days left.

st_max_symbol_pct_of_book.label: Short-term put: max single-name share of the book
st_max_symbol_pct_of_book.description: No new put on a name whose holdings + put collateral already make up this much of the short-term book (holdings + all put collateral). Neel 2026-09-16: SOXL was 36% and V7 was still asking for more.

new_call_min_dte.label: New call: minimum days to expiry
new_call_min_dte.description: A new call goes on this Friday's expiry only if at least this many days remain; otherwise next Friday's. Neel 2026-09-16 (Wednesday): 'not this week, but the end of next week.'

rule_a_up_day_pct.label: Winning call: roll early on an up day of
rule_a_up_day_pct.description: Within the last days of a winning call (fewer than the dip buy-back's minimum), roll as soon as the stock is up at least this much on the day — the bounce is the moment to set the next strike. Otherwise roll Friday. Neel 2026-09-16: TSLA $390 on a +1.3% day; theta timing was a wash, the price path decides.

put_depressed_bonus.label: Put ranking: depressed-name bonus
put_depressed_bonus.description: Multiplier on the yield score for a name at least the mean-reversion threshold below its 10-day average.

runaway_uncap_delta.label: Runaway: uncap calls at delta ≥
runaway_uncap_delta.description: While a runaway thesis is active, a call is bought back only when its delta (chance of finishing in the money, from the name's realized vol, the gap and the days left) is at or above this. Neel 2026-09-16: SPCX \$160 with 2 days left and a \$10 gap is delta 0.08 — a normal call, not a runaway risk; Monday's \$152.50 was 0.39.

lt_wait_rsi.label: Long-term call: wait while RSI below
lt_wait_rsi.description: No new long-term call while the name is oversold — a call sold at the bottom caps the recovery. Restores the RSI half of V6's entry gate (the 'two +3% sessions' half stays retired). Neel 2026-09-16: AVGO RSI 34, still slipping after Monday's buy-back — wait; NVDA RSI 45 — sell.

put_roll_tv_floor.label: ITM put: roll-now time-value floor
put_roll_tv_floor.description: Same as the call rule, mirrored: an in-the-money short put is rolled Thursday for a credit at the same strike; immediately once its time value is at or below this (early-assignment risk). Never pay intrinsic to get out; assignment is the alternative when the shares are wanted and the cash/margin is there.

put_min_premium_per_contract.label: Put: minimum $ per contract
put_min_premium_per_contract.description: A put paying less than this per contract is not worth a slot (IBIT at $61 ranked #3 on 2026-09-17).

st_assign_rsi.label: Short-term ITM call: roll above RSI
st_assign_rsi.description: Thursday of expiry week, roll paying a credit: RSI at or above this → ROLL (overbought, the run is likely to come back under the strike — be patient); below → LET ASSIGN (not stretched, the same money earns more as a put on the next-ranked name). No credit → always LET ASSIGN. Neel, 2026-09-20; 65 is the starting point.

put_only.rule: Bucket C's own names — puts on symbols in neither book (Neel, 2026-09-20: 'things that I will come up with'). If assigned, the shares are short-term book by default.
